column1: # D6's pass conditions for the Modbus/TCP content signature (brief P4-4-E2, D4-90), written before any measurement of it.
# This file decides. Why each row is here: docs/phase4/D6-modbus-signature-conditions.md.
# Rows are judged as docs/phase4/D6-engine-run-pass-conditions.md says (rules 1 to 9, section 3), unless a row says otherwise.
# op and value are a row's threshold, where it has one. Any edit changes this file's SHA-256: test_modbus_signature_conditions.py pins it, and the run checks it against pins.env.

column5: rule

Zeek 9.0.1 with the project's script as approved (D1 on #637), plus the Modbus/TCP content signature and any setting it needs, each named, plus `redef DPD::ignore_violations += { Analyzer::ANALYZER_MODBUS }` if the script carries it. Every row is judged on S0 as one configuration: the signature, its settings and the redef together when they are present. The run records the SHA-256 of every script and signature file S0 loads, and an adoption names those hashes.
Zeek 9.0.1 with the project's script as approved, in the same run, differing from S0 only by the signature, its settings and the redef. The run records its SHA-256s too.
Only when S0 carries the redef: the same script with the signature and without the redef, in the same run. It is reported beside S0 row by row and decides nothing.

S0 names no port (a range, or every port, included), no address and no capture, and holds no value chosen because a GT-PCAP or corpus capture holds it: no transaction ID, unit, length or function code learned from them. A configuration that breaks this fails every det- and held- row as `fail (told the port)`.

A flow is named Modbus by a configuration when any record of that configuration's logs tied to the flow (rule 2) names Modbus: conn.log's `service` holding `modbus`, with or without a leading `-`; any `modbus.log` row; or any row of the project's script's log that names Modbus. `analyzer.log` is not read for this.

Each row is `pass`, `fail` or `unknown`. What did not run is `unknown`, never `pass`. The flows of a capture on which a configuration logs no flow record at all are `unknown (capture not decoded)` and are in no count. A count passes on its own count only, never on silence.

The run counts only when it is dispatched from refs/heads/main with this file, engine-pass-conditions.tsv, the corpus manifest and the corpus labels each equal to its pin in modules/telemetry/experiments/engine-linux/pins.env. Any other run is a rehearsal, and every table it writes says so.

The counted result lists every earlier run of S0 over the corpus, by run ID, and says whether the signature or the redef changed after it. A corpus that S0 ran over before the counted run is reported as seen.
The row of engine-pass-conditions.tsv with capture `modbus-moved-port` and condition `protocol` passes under S0.
The row with capture `modbus-moved-port` and condition `service` (192.168.110.138 tcp/15020) passes under S0.
The row with capture `modbus-moved-port` and condition `function` (function 3 from 192.168.110.131) passes under S0.
The control: the source capture on port 502 passes the same three rows under S0. If it does not, the three det- rows read `fail (also fails on port 502)` and do not pass.

S1 fails the three rows in the same run, as it did in run 43092601088. If S1 passes any of them, something other than the signature finds Modbus on 15020, and the three det- rows read `unknown (the baseline passes too)`.

Every row of engine-pass-conditions.tsv, at its pin, that S1 passes in the same run passes under S0 too. At the pin 38e6c081c7ab62b2b88e8bef1574d136121a3a839f4499d6fe8ba7d7e8acc80e the approved configuration passed 107 of the 110 rows (run 43092601088), so at that pin reg-rows and the three det- rows together ask S0 for 110 of 110.

For each flow the corpus labels `modbus` whose server is on TCP 502 in its source: the capture is moved by tests/integration/gt_pcap/movedport.py to 15020, or, where it already uses 15020, to another port it does not use that is not 20, 21, 23, 102, 502 or 20000, and labelled in the run by modbus_label.py with the pinned tshark. Each of its protocol, service and function rows passes under S0 whenever the same row of the unmoved capture passes under S0. A row that fails on 502 too is `fail (also fails on port 502)`, is listed, and is not counted against S0. A capture that modbus_label.py refuses is listed, and its flows are in no count. A flow whose capture holds no SYN from its client and whose first frame is sent from the server's port is listed as `(roles not recoverable off 502)` and judged on its protocol row only: with no SYN, Zeek swaps the two ends only when the first sender's port is one it holds as a likely server port, which 502 is and a moved port is not (Zeek v9.0.1 TCP.cc lines 55 to 70, analyzer/main.zeek lines 256 and 257; D2's B1 on #642).

For each flow the corpus labels `modbus` whose server is on another port in its source: its protocol and service rows pass under S0, with no control. A flow with no SYN from its client whose first frame is the server's is listed as `(roles not recoverable off 502)` and judged on its protocol row only, as in held-502.

held-502 and held-other together hold at least 5 flows that count (held-502's with a passing control, and every held-other flow), from at least 2 captures other than modbus.pcap. A flow listed as `(roles not recoverable off 502)` does not count. With fewer, both rows are `unknown`.

D2 reads them against the protocol, and D6 against this file, on the PR that adds S0 and at the head that merges, before the counted run. Their text includes any eval function or script code the signature calls. (a) It holds nothing judge-port forbids. (b) It accepts, as a client's first request, every Modbus code that fc-classes/1 lists (1 to 6, 8, 15, 16, 22, 23, 43, 60h, 61h, 62h, 7Dh and 7Eh; modules/detection/netdetect/fcclasses.go at e20a594f), so that a session opened with a write, a control or one of SEL's own codes is not missed. (c) It reads the reassembled stream and not segments: it does not refuse a stream whose first segment holds several ADUs, ends partway through one, or holds a header without its PDU (D2's finding G on #637). (d) It accepts any transaction ID, 0 included, any unit ID from 0 to 255, and any length from 2 to 254 (D2 on #642, from the Modbus specifications, which the project does not hold). (e) If it requires a reply, an exception reply, the request's code plus 80h with an exception code, counts as one. The review also says whether the signature requires anything of the server's reply, and what it does when the first stream it sees is the server's, a response or an exception (D2 on #642).
No flow that the corpus labels `not-modbus`, on any transport, is named Modbus by S0 (judge-named).
fp-flows counts only when at least 300 `not-modbus` TCP flows, each with payload from at least one end, have a flow record under S0. With fewer, fp-flows is `unknown`.

At least 10 of fp-floor's flows, from at least 2 application protocols, are near misses: for one end or the other, the first 8 octets of the stream it sends, as reassembled, have octets 2 and 3 (counting from 0) zero, and octets 4 and 5, read as one big-endian number, at least 2. Zeek's own Modbus parser takes them as a header, so on these flows the signature alone decides. One of the protocols is Modbus RTU framing carried in raw TCP (label-not-modbus): for example a request at address 0 with a quantity of 2 or more, such as 01 03 00 00 00 02 C4 0B (D2's B2 on #642). Synthesized near misses may make up the number and the RTU protocol, each written by a script in this repository and labelled synthesized, and are reported apart from public ones. With fewer, or with no RTU near miss, fp-flows is `unknown`.

The counter runs once more on a copy of the labels in which one flow that S0 names Modbus (modbus.pcap's flow on 502) is relabelled `not-modbus`, and reports exactly one false positive more than fp-flows. If it does not, fp-flows is `unknown`.

GT-PCAP's DNP3 captures (gt-pcap/dnp3/dnp3.sha256), the public captures E-D4-03 read (public-ot-captures/MANIFEST.tsv and engine-linux/extra-captures.tsv), and the additions D4 names under P4-4-E2. No derived capture (the PRP pairs, the moved-port captures) is a member, so no flow is counted twice.
They include IEC 60870-5-104, MMS over TPKT, EtherNet/IP and DNP3, and no one protocol is more than half of fp-floor's flows.

Every capture is public and published by a third party, or synthesized by a script in this repository. None was captured by this project or by the owner, none comes from a site of the owner's or from a network either of them operates, and none is a capture its publisher says was recorded on an operational network. A capture of unknown origin is allowed only as already published, and its label says so, as modbus.pcap's does.

Each source states terms that allow this use, or is used as MANIFEST.tsv's captures are: fetched in the run at a pinned SHA-256 and never committed. A capture is committed only if its terms allow redistribution from a public repository, and D7 confirms that. A source that needs registration, an agreement or a request to its publisher is not used.

The corpus manifest (each capture's name, its URL or its writer, and its SHA-256) and the corpus labels are committed and pinned by SHA-256 in pins.env. D6 confirms them against every corpus- and label- row, and D2 reviews the labels, on that PR before it merges.

The corpus manifest lists what the corpus does not hold, at least each of these it lacks: SEL Fast Message and SEL's other binary protocols, Modbus ASCII framing inside raw TCP, C37.118 over TCP, proprietary engineering-tool protocols, and live capture from a SPAN or TAP port.

One label row per flow of each corpus capture, with: capture, source, l4, src, sport, dst, dport (dst and dport name the server), direction, packets_src, packets_dst, payload_src, payload_dst (payload octets from each end), class, protocol, by_source, by_tshark, and near_miss (fp-near). The server is the end that received the SYN; with no SYN, the end its source names; else the receiver of the first payload, as C13 section 4.1 has it for UDP. A label holds no payload bytes and no host name.

A flow is `modbus` when its source says the capture holds Modbus/TCP, its server port is 502 or a port the source names for Modbus/TCP, and the pinned tshark, told that port is Modbus/TCP, reads at least one request sent to that end.

A flow is `not-modbus` when its source names its protocol as one that is not Modbus, or names the capture's protocols and none of them is Modbus; the pinned tshark with default settings reads no Modbus/TCP on it; and, told the flow's server port is Modbus/TCP, it reads no request to that end that a response from it answers with the same transaction ID and the same function code, or that code plus 80h. Modbus RTU or ASCII framing carried in raw TCP is `not-modbus` for this measurement, whatever its source calls it, when it meets the two tshark checks: C13 and V-M6 name Modbus/TCP, and Zeek's parser misreads RTU framing as an MBAP header (D2's B2 on #642).

Every other flow is `disputed`. Disputed flows are listed in the labels before the run, are in no count, and are named in the report if S0 names one of them Modbus. They are at most 5 in every 100 of the corpus's TCP flows with payload, or D6 does not confirm the corpus.

If S0 carries the redef, the report states beside the result what it removes, on every Modbus flow, on 502 as well as on a moved port: a Modbus parse violation no longer disables the analyzer, no longer removes `modbus` from conn.log's `service`, and writes no analyzer.log row. In Zeek v9.0.1, base/frameworks/analyzer/dpd.zeek lines 87 and 88 return before the analyzer is disabled (line 104) or `analyzer_failed` is raised (lines 100 and 108), so lines 62 and 63 never remove the service and base/frameworks/analyzer/logging.zeek lines 97 to 112 write nothing. So a flow the signature enabled wrongly stays named Modbus for the rest of the connection, is not reported `undecoded`, and leaves no violation in any log. S2's counts beside S0's show what the redef changed in the run.

For S0, S1, and S2 where it runs: every det-, ctl- and reg- row; held-502, held-other and held-count as n of m, with each `also fails on port 502` and each `roles not recoverable off 502` listed; every fp- row; fp-floor's count for each application protocol; the near misses' own count, public and synthesized apart, and the false positives among them; the 95% upper bound on the per-flow false-positive rate, which is 3 divided by fp-floor's count when fp-flows is zero, and the same bound over the near misses alone; and each false positive by capture, labelled protocol and server end, never by its bytes. A measured zero is not reported as a rate of zero.

The signature, as S0, is adopted only when every row with a threshold (op and value) holds in one counted run (judge-counted). Any row that does not hold, or is `unknown`, means it is not adopted. D6 proposes this row; D1 states the threshold on the PR that adds this file, before it merges.

Adoption does not close HR-22 by itself (D3 writes it under P4-4-L6, and D1 decides when it closes). The `undecoded` signal with `unknown-pair` is still owed before the gate (D4-90). No row shows a session that opens with a code outside fc-classes/1, live capture, or anything corpus-not-held lists, and Modbus RTU or ASCII framing inside raw TCP, which this measurement classes `not-modbus`, is not identified as Modbus by any row.

column5: A signature changed after a counted run that did not adopt it is measured in a new counted run against this file unchanged, with judge-seen's seen corpus stated. D1 decides whether a seen corpus is enough.
